Distribution Malaysia, Philippines and Singapore. Habitat and seasonal occurrence This is one of the most common species of Elaphropeza in Singapore, with records from all forest types. The species was already known in Singapore from Bukit Timah, Nee Soon, Chek Jawa and Sime forest. Here we add records from Semakau and Kranji. Elaphropeza biuncinata is present throughout the year. In the first half of the year there are short, small peaks nearly every month that probably reflect a onemonth generation time interval. It is abundant and continuously present from the beginning of August until mid of December. The sex ratio is almost 1 / 1 suggesting a similar activity pattern for females and males.
